We use Taylor's formula in the form

$$
f(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+⋯,
$$

with $f(x)=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ and $a=\pi .$ 

Calculating the necessary derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x \\ f(\pi ) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\pi )=-1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(\pi ) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\pi )\operatorname{tan}⁡(\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x{tan}^{2}⁡x+{sec}^{3}⁡x \\ {f}^{″}(\pi ) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\pi ){tan}^{2}⁡(\pi )+{sec}^{3}⁡(\pi )=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the Taylor series is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡x & =-1+(0)(x-\pi )+\frac{(-1)}{2!}(x-\pi )^{2}+⋯ \\  & =-1-\frac{1}{2}(x-\pi )^{2}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $x=\pi +0.2$ into the above to approximate $\operatorname{sec}⁡(\pi +0.2).$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡(\pi +0.2) & ≈-1-\frac{1}{2}{(\pi +0.2-\pi )}^{2} \\  & =-1-\frac{1}{2}(0.2)^{2} \\  & =-1-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{25}) \\  & =-1-\frac{1}{50} \\  & =-\frac{51}{50}.\end{aligned}
$$
